Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and appreciate the detailed context on the chat use case. Recapping the SLOs and the ask from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Summary (what we heard)
- P95 latency target: 250–300ms for single-turn generation on short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: responses must stream token-by-token with first-byte latency < 120ms for chat UX.
- Throughput: sustained 400–500 req/s during business hours; spike concurrency up to ~350 for promotions.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrency ~120, peak 350; average response length ~120 tokens, 95th token length ~450 tokens.

Proposed next steps
1) Please share a representative 1–2 day sample of production traffic (ndjson) with tokenized inputs or average token counts. If you prefer, we can provide a sanitized template.
2) Approve a short benchmarking window (48 hours) where Redwood runs workload tests against a Dedicated sandbox with your sample traffic. We'll test 3 config variants (high-throughput batching, quantized model variant, and a streaming-optimized variant).
3) We'll deliver a SLO worksheet + cost/performance recommendations and a suggested rollout plan (canary -> gradual traffic ramp).

Attachments: SLO_requirements_novaretail_v2.pdf, SLO_worksheet.xlsx

Quick note on likely levers we expect to consider: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts, model quantization (int8/int4 depending on quality), and using a smaller model variant for low-latency user journeys while routing higher-compute flows to larger models. I'll share more specifics once we have the sample traffic.

Are you ok with the 48-hour benchmarking window (we'd need access details for a test endpoint and an S3/HTTP location for the sample traffic)?

Thanks,

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Lena — that data will be perfect. Quick follow-up with concrete levers + what we'll test in the 48-hour benchmark so expectations are clear: 

Planned cost/performance levers to evaluate
- Continuous batching: dynamic batching tuned to p95 tail, with a low-latency cutoff for high-priority requests. This often reduces per-token cost by 20–40% at modest latency impact for high-throughput workloads.
- Prefix / KV caching: customer-level prompt caching for repeated prefixes (e.g., product metadata, system prompts) to avoid recomputation for common flows. Expected 10–30% token savings depending on repeat rate.
- Quantization profiles: test int8 and int4 (where quality permits) on selected models. For many classification/generation tasks, int8 provides a favorable latency/cost tradeoff; int4 can be viable for lower-risk journeys.
- Model variants & routing: evaluate a 7B or quantized 13B as a low-latency variant for short-turn chat while routing longer/high-precision flows to a 13B/70B instance. Smart routing can keep perceived latency low while preserving accuracy on complex queries.
- Streaming optimizations: chunked token flushes and earlier first-byte emit to meet first-byte goals (<150ms) even when overall generation runs longer.
- Autoscaling policy: pre-warm pools for predictable promotional spikes and fast autoscale for unexpected surges.

What we'll deliver after the benchmark
- P50/P95/P99 latency curves by model/config and token length buckets.
- Token-level cost and request-level cost breakdowns (before/after cache/batching).
- Recommended Dedicated sizing (GPU counts + instance types) with committed vs burst cost estimates.
- Concrete rollout plan: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with fallback policies.

To run the tests we need:
- The 48-hour sample (S3 or secure Drive link) with anonymized user IDs and token counts.
- A test API key / hostname or permission to provision a sandbox with identical routing rules.

If you confirm, we'll schedule the benchmark next week (48-hour window) and aim to share results within 72 hours of test completion.

Attaching Redwood_cost_levers_summary.pdf for quick reference.

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi Lena / Tom — copying in Marissa and Priyom for ops and model tuning. Quick preliminary cost note ahead of the benchmark results so you have a ballpark to discuss internally: 

Prelim cost ranges (very rough)
- Hosted API (burstable): expected $0.08–$0.15 per 1k tokens for streaming-optimized models at your target latency, depending on traffic shape and caching effectiveness.
- Dedicated baseline (monthly committed): for sustained 400–500 req/s with peak concurrency ~350, expect a dedicated pool sizing in the range of X GPU (we'll confirm exact instance types after benchmarking) with a committed monthly price that typically yields 30–50% lower per-token costs vs hosted at scale.

Operational asks
- For the Dedicated estimate we need the sample traffic + a 7-day historic peak (if available) so we can size pre-warmed pools appropriately.
- For security/compliance: if you need Private (VPC) deployment for data residency we can include that pricing as an add-on; please flag now.

I'll follow up with a more concrete Dedicated sizing once the benchmark completes. Looking forward to the test data — thanks for moving quickly on this.
